title: mut.channel_plane_color_field
mutation_directive: Channel plane-based color-field art. Render the form as PLANES (translucent quads / sheets / volumetric layers), not points or lines. Use THREE.InstancedMesh of small PlaneGeometry instances, each oriented either billboarded-to-camera or aligned to a local normal field. Pick one artist as the aesthetic anchor: Mark Rothko — large stacked horizontal rectangles, soft soaked edges, emotional weight from minimal vocabulary. 2-3 dominant color bands; bottom band weight, top band lightness; 'soaked-stain' edges via per-instance position jitter at band borders. Vermilion-on-maroon, plum-on-orange, slate-on-rust.. Stay near monochrome or two-color (saturated, low value contrast). Use additive blending with low per-instance opacity (0.04-0.10) so OVERLAP IS THE COMPOSITION — the deeper the stack of overlapping planes, the brighter and more saturated the local color. The piece should feel like LIGHT, not particles — Turrell's 'we eat light, drink it through our skins.'
